defense_analyst.prose: Carolina blitzes often: it sends five or more rushers on 35.6% of dropbacks [dc1] over 306 plays [dc2], averaging 4.4 rushers per dropback [dc3], and its pressure proxy (sacks plus QB hits) is 10.5% [dc4]. That aggression has not come cheap in coverage: it allows 0.07 EPA per pass play [dc5] and explosive passes on 5.2% of attempts [dc6]. Expect New Orleans to test those looks with quick game and RPO answers rather than deep shots. The run defense is the stronger unit: it allows -0.03 EPA per run play [dc7] over 210 runs [dc8], with 6.5 defenders in the box on average [dc9]. New Orleans will have to win on the ground only if it can get Carolina out of its light boxes, so use the run to set up the pass. Third down is the soft spot: Carolina allows conversions on 47.7% of 107 third-down plays [dc10][dc11], which ranks 29th of 32 [dc12] where lower is better. New Orleans uses play action rarely, ranking 31st in play-action rate [dc13], and screens least of all, 32nd [dc14]. Its motion usage ranks 11th [dc15] and RPO usage 20th [dc16], so motion and RPO looks are the likely third-down threats. Carolina has allowed touchdowns on 75.0% of 24 red-zone drives [dc17][dc18], but that sample is small and should be read cautiously.
